data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's claim concedes that 'checklists only succeed in additive verification tasks,' yet the problem asks the arguer to take a position on whether a panel of non-experts will 'on average' outperform a single expert. By restricting the claim's scope solely to complex/emergent tasks, SRC_001 leaves entirely undefended the larger population of 'tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes' that includes additive tasks. A problem about the average across the full population cannot be answered by an argument that covers only one subset of that population and grants the contrary outcome for the other subset, since the average depends on the proportion and weight of the two subsets — a quantity SRC_001 never addresses.
